There are two kinds of leafy greens that you can do this with:

- perennials, which will keep going for several years

- annuals, which last for less than a year, but you can keep harvesting for a few months.

With perennials, you are better off planting in the ground, so they can establish a good root system and feed themselves. If you grow them in a container, you will need to change out the soil every couple of years and prune the roots to keep them vigorous. Perennials have (usually) tougher leaves - you can harvest tender new growth, but that means lesser volume of harvest, and a potentially more stunted plant. Good examples of these are perennial Collard greens, lacinato Kale, curled Kale, Gynura procumbens, New zealand spinach, Moringa etc.

Annuals need to be regrown each year (although some of them reseed themselves) - but you can plant them in containers, and there is a huge variety of them so you can get a lot of different tastes, flavors and nutritional profiles in a small space. What you need to look for is 'cut-and-come-again' varieties, which will survive an occasional harvest without dying. A good rule of thumb is to only harvest about 1/3 of the leaves from each plant. The best ones that produce a lot of leaves are Swiss chard, mustard greens, arugula, daikon radish greens and some varieties of amaranth greens. There are many varieties of lettuce - what you need are "leaf" lettuce, and not "head" lettuce. Spinach is a little finicky to grow, but a good option - you do have to plant a lot of it to get a decent harvest.

You can also try self-seeding annuals that are a little uncommon - purslane, french sorrel, etc. This category gives you the extended harvest benefit of a perennial, but also the tender and more flavorful aspects of annuals.

Lastly, "leafy greens" are not just leaf plants. There are many vegetables whose leaves are not only edible, but are very high in nutrient value. You harvest a few leaves, and then get to pick a vegetable as well. e.g. radishes, carrots, beets, turnips, kohlrabi, grapes, taro-root, sweet-potato, etc. Just make sure you don't eat tomato, eggplant of potato leaves.
